tasks.title: Unblock the pilot customer's migration
tasks.excerpt: The pilot team is waiting on our import mapping. They can still join today's launch if we resolve it before 11:00.
tasks.rationale: A customer outcome with a narrow window. The 52-point value is an editable judgment about keeping the pilot on track.

tasks.title: Find a cost code for an internal invoice
tasks.excerpt: Could you send the cost code before 09:45? My spreadsheet is open now. Tomorrow's processing run is also fine.
tasks.rationale: An early requested cutoff, but low cost to defer. Its six points make the difference between urgency and value explicit.

tasks.title: Polish an optional launch caption
tasks.excerpt: A final wordsmithing pass by 10:30 would be lovely. The approved caption is ready if you cannot get to it.
tasks.rationale: The approved fallback already works. This five-point improvement can consume the morning slot needed by a customer.

tasks.title: Verify the release candidate
tasks.excerpt: Please verify the import and billing paths by 13:45. Your signed checklist is the input to the rollback rehearsal.
tasks.rationale: The first link in the release chain. Its direct score understates its importance because two downstream tasks depend on it.

tasks.title: Rehearse the rollback
tasks.excerpt: Once the candidate passes, run the rollback rehearsal and record the result by 14:30. We need it before the release handoff.
tasks.rationale: A concrete dependency on candidate verification. The 35-minute block cannot be split around lunch.

tasks.title: Complete the launch handoff
tasks.excerpt: After QA and the rollback rehearsal, package the release notes, owner checklist, and go/no-go summary before the 15:00 sync.
tasks.rationale: The highest-value deliverable requires both earlier links. Planning only by a task's own score or cutoff can lose the entire chain.

tasks.title: Prepare the partner's launch packet
tasks.excerpt: The final partner assets arrive at 13:00. Please assemble their packet between then and our 15:00 meeting.
tasks.rationale: A useful afternoon commitment with an explicit earliest start. It cannot be pulled into a convenient morning gap.

tasks.title: Resolve a customer's renewal concern
tasks.excerpt: A customer needs a clear rollout answer before their 16:30 review. Please read the notes and prepare a specific response.
tasks.rationale: A 46-point customer outcome that benefits from staying in the same workstream as the partner packet.

tasks.title: Check the first-hour adoption snapshot
tasks.excerpt: The first reliable export will be available at 16:00. Spend 25 minutes checking adoption and flagging anomalies before 17:00.
tasks.rationale: A time-gated task that gives a late-day gap a purpose. The planner must wait for the data even if capacity remains earlier.

tasks.title: Finish the vendor approval packet
tasks.excerpt: Legal has not returned the signed addendum. Once it arrives, finishing the approval packet should take 20 minutes.
tasks.rationale: More available time cannot resolve missing external approval. The blocker also prevents the dependent seat purchase.
tasks.blocked: Waiting for Legal's signed addendum; no arrival time is confirmed.

tasks.title: Arrange the support team's vendor seats
tasks.excerpt: After the vendor approval packet is complete, assemble the seat order and the team's access instructions.
tasks.rationale: An indirect blocker: this work is valuable, but cannot be scheduled while its approval dependency is unresolved.

tasks.title: Tidy labels before the inbox review
tasks.excerpt: If you can, clean up the old labels for the 11:30 review. We can review the current structure if launch work takes priority.
tasks.rationale: A 35-minute cosmetic improvement with a nine-point score. Its early cutoff makes it tempting for an urgency-first plan.
